newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait Central Bank orders anti-laundering measures.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait Central Bank orders anti-laundering measures.

text.p: Kuwait's Central Bank has ordered domestic banks to take measures to avoid money laundering, the bank's governor was quoted on Sunday as saying.
The Central Bank has issued measures ..."to close the way for any attempts to carry out money laundering," Governor Sheikh Salem Abdul-Aziz al-Sabah told al-Rai al-Aam newspaper.

Banks are required to check clients' identities and the nature of their business, he said. They have to inform the Central Bank of all cash deposits exceeding $33,000 and provide authorities with information about "irregular" and large transactions.
"The imposed measures...have resulted in preventing some suspicious transactions," he added without elaboration. "It is not true that Kuwaiti banks are involved in money laundering."
Kuwait has six commercial banks, two specialised banks, an Islamic finance institution and a branch of a Bahrain-based bank.
